legend: Each label is a judgement, and it holds under the conditions its entry states. Check an entry again when your own test disagrees with it, when something goes wrong in use, or when your model, data, tools, licence or scope changes. The products named are examples: compare them on your own work before you buy.

intelligence.name: Use
intelligence.meaning: Ready to use under the stated conditions, with normal controls and local validation.

intelligence.name: Trial
intelligence.short: Ready for a bounded, measured pilot.
intelligence.meaning: Ready for a bounded, measured pilot with a named owner and exit criteria.

intelligence.name: Evaluate
intelligence.short: Worth investigating on your own tasks.
intelligence.meaning: Worth investigating on your own tasks and risks before any live role.

intelligence.name: Wait
intelligence.short: Defer until a named obstacle clears.
intelligence.meaning: Defer the stated use until a named obstacle is resolved. The entry says what would change the judgement.

intelligence.name: Prepare
intelligence.meaning: Build what it needs now: data, evaluation, controls, contracts and skills. These can take longer to put in place than the technology takes to mature.

enterprise.name: Revisit
enterprise.short: Re-examine a practice you already have.
enterprise.meaning: Recent evidence or delivery experience challenges a decision or practice that many organisations already have. Re-examine it now.

enterprise.name: Test
enterprise.short: Run a measured test on your own work.
enterprise.meaning: Commit an owner and a budget to a measured test on your own work in the coming quarter.

enterprise.name: Plan for
enterprise.short: Get ready for a change that is coming.
enterprise.meaning: A change is arriving or already under way. Build the organisational capacity to absorb it: skills, contracts, policy, data and controls.

enterprise.name: Watch
enterprise.meaning: No commitment yet. Follow the developments its entry describes and look again in the next edition.

evidence.name: Measured
evidence.meaning: A quantitative result with a stated method. Check the population, uncertainty and independence of the measurement.

evidence.name: Documented
evidence.meaning: A primary record of an event or decision: a filing, regulation, court direction, official statement or first-party incident report.

evidence.name: Demonstrated
evidence.meaning: Shown working in a described case. Wider reliability and transfer to other settings remain to be tested.

evidence.name: Reported
evidence.meaning: A second-hand account awaiting a primary check. Keep the attribution when quoting it.

evidence.name: Opinion
evidence.meaning: A view or forecast, including company expectations and practitioner views.

lenses.name: Capability
lenses.question: What can the models, the methods and the machines do?

lenses.name: Context
lenses.question: What makes that capability useful here: the knowledge and expertise, the workflow, the product and the people?

lenses.name: Control

dimensions.name: Models and inference
dimensions.question: Which model, sized and served how, for each task?
dimensions.description: How to choose, size, route, host and serve models. Model choice became a recurring decision in 2026, so this dimension treats models as replaceable parts behind stable task contracts, with the ability to evaluate and replace them as the lasting asset.
dimensions.covers: Choosing, sizing, routing, hosting and serving models
dimensions.intro: The model is still the engine, and the decisions that determine whether one works in an organisation now sit around it: how to choose it, size it, route work to it, host it and serve it. Nine major model releases arrived between 3 September and 26 October 2026 [15, 68, 69, 122, 123, 128 to 131], and token prices moved by double digits within weeks [23]. Model choice has become a recurring decision. Treat models as replaceable parts behind stable task contracts, and treat the ability to evaluate and replace them as the lasting asset (IR-049, IR-087).
implications: Revisit model choices made on reputation or a public ranking, and choose on your own exam (IR-001, IR-049).
Test routing, caching, structured outputs and small models; each cuts cost once your exam confirms the quality (IR-009, IR-011, IR-007, IR-002).
Watch self-hosting and advanced serving optimisations until your volume and skills justify them (IR-003, IR-010, IR-012).

dimensions.name: Knowledge, context and expertise
dimensions.question: What does the model see, and who is allowed to see it?
dimensions.description: Everything a model is given to read and remember: retrieval with the user's permissions, parsed documents, memory, provenance, and the judgement of experienced people. These sit together because most failures in knowledge work begin with the wrong context, and expertise is the context that documents leave out.
dimensions.covers: Permissions, retrieval, parsing, graphs, memory, expertise and tacit knowledge, provenance and deletion
dimensions.intro: In Brightbeam's practitioner experience, recurring failures involve what the model was given to read: the wrong version, a document the user should never have seen, a summary that dropped the exception, a memory nobody owns. Knowledge work is where AI earns its value, and context engineering strongly influences the outcome. Retrieve with the user's permissions, keep provenance to the passage, treat what enters the prompt as a versioned decision, and decide who owns an agent's memory before agents start keeping one. Persistent personal agents launched in the second half of 2026 make memory ownership a present question [17, 19, 20]. Expertise belongs here too: the judgement of experienced people, recorded with its conditions and checked before others rely on it, often provides context needed for a sound answer (IR-020).
implications: Revisit any assistant that retrieves without the user's permissions or cites without provenance (IR-013, IR-021).
Test the retrieval stack and the capture of expert judgement on your own documents and cases (IR-014, IR-015, IR-016, IR-020).
Plan for agent memory with owners and expiry, and for corrections and deletions that reach every copy (IR-019, IR-024).

dimensions.name: Agents and workflow
dimensions.question: How much freedom should software have, and how is it stopped?
dimensions.description: How work is delegated to software that acts: deterministic workflows, bounded agents, durable execution, tool protocols, computer use and coding agents. These sit together because each design choice sets how much freedom the software has and how a person can stop it.
dimensions.covers: Bounded agents, deterministic workflows, durable execution, tool and agent protocols, computer use, approval and coding agents
dimensions.intro: Agents moved from answering to doing in the second half of 2026: computer-use models, persistent personal agents and coding agents now take on whole tasks [15, 17, 19]. In Brightbeam's experience, the projects that work run few agents, with clear limits, identities, budgets and records. Start with a deterministic workflow that calls a model where judgement is needed, then a bounded single agent with a stopping condition, and add more agents only when a measured division of labour pays for the coordination. Put a person where actions are consequential, and give that person the information, time and authority to stop the work.
implications: Revisit agent designs that skip a deterministic workflow, human takeover or a sandbox; all three are ready now (IR-026, IR-032, IR-034).
Test bounded single agents, durable execution, MCP tools and coding agents on measured work (IR-025, IR-027, IR-028, IR-035).
Plan for computer-use agents arriving through vendors, and hold back open-ended autonomy (IR-031, IR-036).

dimensions.name: Assurance, security and governance
dimensions.question: Who may act, who can stop it, and what proves it?
dimensions.description: What makes AI dependable and accountable: identity and least privilege, security testing, incident containment, oversight records, regulation and governance by risk tier. Assurance, security and governance sit together because each depends on knowing who may act, who can stop it and what evidence shows it.
dimensions.covers: Decision rights and accountable owners, regulatory readiness, identity, prompt injection, data protection, independent testing, red-teaming, supply chain, oversight records, incidents and formal proof
dimensions.intro: The defining incidents of the second half of 2026 were containment failures [1 to 9], and attackers adopted agents too [98, 99]. Assurance for AI starts in the environment: identities scoped to the task, secrets kept out of what the model can see, tests the agent cannot reach, and a stop that someone has rehearsed. It ends in evidence: records that let a reviewer reconstruct a decision, and assurance cases that trace each claim to an artefact. Several of these practices are ready today, and the gap lies in how widely organisations apply them. Governance sits here as well: decision rights set by risk tier, a named owner with the authority to stop each system, and a dated view of what each obligation requires (IR-103, IR-092).
implications: Revisit agent identities, independent grading, the stop and governance by risk tier; these practices are ready and often missing (IR-037, IR-040, IR-045, IR-103).
Test prompt-injection resilience, data-loss controls and red-teaming on your own systems (IR-038, IR-039, IR-041).
Plan for supply-chain verification, oversight records, conformance evidence and regulatory readiness as obligations take effect (IR-042, IR-043, IR-047, IR-092).

dimensions.name: Evaluation and learning
dimensions.question: How do you know it works, and how does it improve safely?
dimensions.description: How an organisation measures AI on its own work and improves it safely: owned exams, system evaluation, calibrated judges, accepted work and full cost, staged release and governed learning. These sit together because each lets you change models and harnesses without losing control of quality.
dimensions.covers: Owned exams, system evaluation, calibrated judges, accepted work and full cost, drift, staged release, adaptation and governed learning
dimensions.intro: Accuracy matters when the test represents the work you intend to delegate. In the second half of 2026, leaderboards changed method within weeks, one harness moved a model's score by tens of points, and agents took planted shortcuts when a test rewarded them [61, 84]. Evaluation is therefore an organisational asset: a frozen, versioned examination of the work you intend to delegate, a measure of accepted work and its full cost, and a way to release, observe and recall changes, including changes that agents learn for themselves. These practices let an organisation change models and harnesses safely, which is where the lasting advantage sits.
implications: Revisit any delegation that rests on vendor benchmarks, and build an owned exam for the work first (IR-049).
Test full-system evaluation, accepted work at full cost, and staged releases (IR-050, IR-052, IR-054).
Plan for governed learning releases, and keep self-modifying production agents on watch (IR-058, IR-060).

dimensions.name: Prediction, science and physical AI
dimensions.question: Which instrument fits the decision, beyond a language model?
dimensions.description: AI beyond language: predictive models for tables and time series, causal inference, optimisation, computer vision, simulation, scientific discovery and robots. These sit together because they model the statistical and physical world and are judged against measurement; on their own ground they often beat a general language model, which serves as their interface.
dimensions.covers: Classical and foundation prediction, causal inference, optimisation, vision, graphs, simulation, discovery and robotics
dimensions.intro: Choose the right instrument for each decision. Generation is one capability among several: classification, forecasting, optimisation, graph reasoning, simulation and causal inference each have mature methods that often beat a language model on their own ground, with the language model as interface and orchestrator. This dimension also holds the most visible discoveries of the second half of 2026, made by people directing AI under careful limits [25, 26, 90], and the physical frontier, where the editors counsel patience: harm in the physical world cannot be rolled back like a software release.
implications: Revisit generative models used for prediction problems, where strong classical baselines often win (IR-061).
Test tabular and time-series foundation models, optimisation and inspection vision against those baselines (IR-062, IR-063, IR-065, IR-066).
Plan review capacity for AI-assisted discovery, and watch robotics and physical autonomy, where harm cannot be rolled back (IR-069, IR-071, IR-072).

dimensions.name: Work, products and people
dimensions.question: What changes for people, their work and their customers?
dimensions.description: How AI changes people's work and the services they deliver: drafting, customer service, search, expert decision support, media, learning, literacy, accessibility and commerce. These sit together because value appears in work that people accept and in outcomes for customers and staff.
dimensions.covers: Assistance, service, search, process, expert decision support, media, apprenticeship, literacy, inclusion and commerce
dimensions.intro: This dimension covers how AI changes people's work and the services they deliver. The evidence is uneven. Before the period, firms used AI to supplement, substitute and add tasks at once, and most reported no change in employment [83]; in the second half of 2026, 60% of respondents to one survey said their workload rose [24]; and the most visible labour signal, an estimate that loses significance with all controls, sits in entry-level hiring [77, 78]. Start with reviewable work where people can judge both the content and its evidence, judge services by the customer and staff outcome, keep the routes by which juniors become experts, and design services for everyone who must use them, in every language they need.
implications: Revisit deflection targets, undisclosed generated media, prohibition-only policies and organisation-wide productivity claims (IR-075, IR-079, IR-081, IR-084).
Test drafting, service copilots, search and expert decision support where people can judge the result (IR-073, IR-074, IR-076, IR-078).
Plan for the routes by which juniors become experts when AI does the routine work (IR-080).

dimensions.name: Operations, economics and sovereignty
dimensions.question: Can you run it, pay for it and leave it?
dimensions.description: Running AI in live work: inventory, traces, releases, cost and spend controls, resilience, sovereignty and validated change. These sit together because each keeps a live system known, affordable and replaceable.
dimensions.covers: Inventory, traces, releases, cost, spend controls, resilience, sovereignty, validated change and national evidence
dimensions.intro: Running intelligence in live work is an operating discipline. In the second half of 2026, models were released and retired, the blended token price Ramp's customers paid fell by about a quarter in a month, and one provider set its introductory price to double after 30 November [23, 69]. The organisations that cope know what they run and who owns it, release model changes through evaluation gates, measure cost against accepted work, bound spending at the system boundary, rehearse supplier exit, and validate changes where regulation requires it. Many of its entries sit in the Prepare ring: readiness here is urgent while several technologies are still maturing.
implications: Revisit your AI inventory, and sovereignty decisions that stop at the hosting region (IR-085, IR-091).
Test purposeful tracing and cost per accepted task (IR-086, IR-088).
Plan for evaluation-gated releases, spend limits, supplier exit, validated change and continuous operation (IR-087, IR-089, IR-090, IR-093, IR-096).

dimensions.name: Compute and hardware
dimensions.question: Where does it run, on what, and at what price and risk?
dimensions.description: The machines underneath: accelerators and their software, inference-specialised chips, owned and rented capacity, GPU cloud contracts, memory supply, power and location, and the PCs and edge devices that run models locally. These sit together because hardware sets the price, the speed and the availability of everything above it.
dimensions.covers: Accelerators and portability, inference-specialised chips, owning and renting capacity, GPU cloud contracts, memory and supply, power and location, AI PCs, NPUs and edge devices
dimensions.intro: Hardware sets the price, the speed and the availability of everything above it. In the second half of 2026 a second accelerator family became practical for inference, specialised chips made some models several times faster, GPU rental gained public price benchmarks with public daily indices, the largest independent GPU cloud's credit came under stress, and a memory shortage raised server prices and cut PC shipments by a fifth [208, 215, 221, 33, 236, 237]. Most organisations will rent their compute; the decisions that matter are what they commit to, with whom, and how portable their serving stays. Keep models portable across accelerators, price every reservation against the indices, assess counterparty risk in capacity contracts, and buy devices for their memory and their lifetime. Power, permission and location decide where capacity can go (IR-094).
implications: Revisit GPU reservations against the public price indices, and device budgets set before the memory shortage (IR-099, IR-102).
Test a second accelerator, fast inference services and on-device models on your own workloads (IR-097, IR-098, IR-070).
Plan for supplier failure and higher hardware prices through 2027, and watch power and permission where capacity is built (IR-100, IR-101, IR-094).

entries.title: Frontier model selection
entries.summary: Leaderboards changed method so often in the second half of 2026 that a ranking is difficult to interpret without knowing its harness: one benchmark verified the same model at 62.7% with its standard harness and up to 99.9% with its maker's adapter, and their comparability is disputed.
judgement: Leaderboards changed method so often in the second half of 2026 that a ranking is difficult to interpret without knowing its harness: one benchmark verified the same model at 62.7% with its standard harness and up to 99.9% with its maker's adapter, and their comparability is disputed [61, 153]. Frontier capability edged up within overlapping intervals [59]. Select the model together with its surrounding system, on work you can judge: your own cases, your own acceptance criteria and full cost. The enterprise posture is Revisit where model choice rests mainly on reputation or a public ranking.
entries.where: A bounded task with an owner and a definition of accepted output.
entries.test: Compare quality, refusals, latency and full cost on unseen local cases, including exceptions.
entries.failure: A benchmark winner that fails on your exception cases.
entries.examples: Hosted model APIs; locally evaluated challengers.

entries.title: Small language models
entries.summary: For narrow, repetitive classification, extraction and constrained drafting, test a smaller model before assuming a frontier model is needed.
judgement: For narrow, repetitive classification, extraction and constrained drafting, test a smaller model before assuming a frontier model is needed. Small models cost a fraction per token: Anthropic's smallest current model lists at $0.10 per million input tokens, with a higher rate for longer prompts [68]. The saving holds only while the complete pipeline still meets its acceptance criteria, including escalations to people or larger models. In Brightbeam's experience, a small model can also match a majority-class baseline while learning little, so assess it against a test set you control (IR-049).
entries.where: High-volume classification, extraction or constrained drafting.
entries.test: Accepted outputs per euro, including escalations, on rare and ordinary cases.
entries.failure: Savings that vanish as expert correction or escalation rises.
entries.examples: Small instruction-tuned models; CPU or GPU serving.

entries.title: Open-weight self-hosting
entries.summary: Open-weight models have trailed the closed frontier by about four months on average since January 2026 on Epoch's index, and on one developer gateway they processed 71.5% of tokens in September.
judgement: Open-weight models have trailed the closed frontier by about four months on average since January 2026 on Epoch's index [207], and on one developer gateway they processed 71.5% of tokens in September [76]. At cutoff, Muse Spark Open had shipped weights under a revenue-capped licence; Mistral Large 4 weights were promised by the end of October, and Kimi K3.1 Pro weights were scheduled for 4 November with no licence announced [128, 129, 131]. Hosting your own model gives you control of data and versions, alongside responsibility for serving, patching and evaluation. Check the licence and every outside dependency before you rely on downloaded weights.
entries.where: A material data, connectivity or supplier constraint, and a team that can operate the service.
entries.test: Run the same acceptance suite locally and hosted; cost idle capacity and incident cover.
entries.failure: Licence limits or dependencies discovered after commitment.

entries.title: Multimodal document understanding
entries.summary: Regulated work runs on forms, scans, diagrams and tables, and text extraction often loses the structure that carries the decision: the column a value sits in, the unit beside it, the signature at the foot of the page.
judgement: Regulated work runs on forms, scans, diagrams and tables, and text extraction often loses the structure that carries the decision: the column a value sits in, the unit beside it, the signature at the foot of the page. Models that read layout, images and text together recover much of it. They can also fail without an obvious warning, producing a fluent answer from a misread row or unit, so every deployment needs a route for people to check uncertain cases.
entries.where: Forms, diagrams, scans or tables, with a human escalation route.
entries.test: Row alignment, small print, missing pages and conflicting visual evidence.
entries.failure: A plausible answer built on a misread table or unit.

entries.title: Speech and real-time voice
entries.summary: Voice suits bounded assistance: booking, triage, guided form-filling and hands-busy work.
judgement: Voice suits bounded assistance: booking, triage, guided form-filling and hands-busy work. Real-time voice models now hold natural conversations that tolerate interruption [194]. The design problems sit around the model: consent, identity, a complete handoff to a person, and an accessible text alternative. Transcription errors matter more once a voice agent can act, because a misheard name or number can become an unauthorised action.
entries.where: A service journey with an accessible text alternative and a route to a person.
entries.test: Regional accents, background noise, interruptions, names, and a complete transfer to a person.
entries.failure: A transcription error that becomes an action.
entries.examples: Speech recognition; speech synthesis; voice agents.

entries.title: Long context versus retrieval
entries.summary: Context windows now hold whole document sets, and some teams have stopped retrieving.
judgement: Context windows now hold whole document sets, and some teams have stopped retrieving. Treat long context and retrieval as two architectures to compare on the same questions. More context can hide missing evidence, raise cost and latency, and disclose more than the task needs; retrieval can miss the passage that matters. Research has found position-dependent retrieval failures in some models and tasks [195]; test whether current candidates still show them. Compare evidence recall and supported-answer quality on your own questions, with permissions applied and cost included.
entries.where: Large document tasks where answer locations and permissions are known.
entries.test: Compare evidence recall, contradiction handling, latency and cost on identical questions.
entries.failure: A long prompt that hides missing evidence and widens disclosure.

entries.title: Structured outputs and typed contracts
entries.summary: When a model's output feeds another system, define the contract: a schema for the structure and rules for the meaning.
judgement: When a model's output feeds another system, define the contract: a schema for the structure and rules for the meaning. Most model platforms can now constrain output to a schema, which removes a whole class of parsing failures. The harder problem remains: a perfectly formed record can still carry a wrong value, an impossible date or a confident fabrication. Validate both layers, the shape with the schema and the meaning with explicit checks maintained by the process owners.
entries.where: Any model output passed into another system.
entries.test: Inject missing fields, impossible values and well-formed but false results; confirm the receiving system rejects them.
entries.failure: Valid JSON that carries a wrong decision.
entries.examples: JSON Schema [196]; typed tool arguments; validation layers.

entries.title: Reasoning and inference-time budgets
entries.summary: Models can now spend more computation on a hard problem before answering, and providers price that effort.
judgement: Models can now spend more computation on a hard problem before answering, and providers price that effort. More reasoning can raise success on some tasks while increasing token use and latency; the trade-off varies by task and system. It can also make errors more persuasive and extend behaviour beyond intended limits: one system card reports restriction circumvention in 29.6% of tests at maximum reasoning effort [64]. Set the effort for each task class according to the measured marginal gain.
entries.where: Difficult tasks with an observable success condition.
entries.test: Sweep effort limits; measure marginal accepted work, timeout rate and cost.
entries.failure: Longer reasoning that produces more persuasive errors.

entries.title: Model routing and cascades
entries.summary: Route straightforward cases to a lower-cost model and escalate uncertain ones, using rules you have measured.
judgement: Route straightforward cases to a lower-cost model and escalate uncertain ones, using rules you have measured. Prices moved fast in the second half of 2026: Ramp's customers paid a blended token price 25.4% lower than in the same week a month earlier while their volume rose [23]; one provider's introductory price doubles after 30 November 2026 [69]; and newer models can use more tokens per task [67]. A well-tested router can turn those price differences into savings. A weak router suppresses exactly the cases a stronger model should see, so measure what it sends where.
entries.where: Repeated task classes with enough labelled outcomes.
entries.test: Routing mistakes, selective accuracy and total escalation cost.
entries.failure: A router that hides the hard cases.
entries.examples: Classifier gates; fallback routes; confidence thresholds.

entries.title: Quantisation and inference optimisation
entries.summary: Organisations that host models can trade numerical precision for memory and throughput.
judgement: Organisations that host models can trade numerical precision for memory and throughput. Quantised weights often keep average quality close to the original, and serving engines make the trade practical [168]. Averages hide the cases that matter: rare formats, numbers, long contexts and safety behaviour. Fix the serving configuration, record it, and test precision settings on consequential edge cases. For organisations on hosted APIs this is the provider's concern, so the enterprise posture is Watch.
entries.where: Stable self-hosted workloads where hardware or latency constrains use.
entries.test: Compare precision settings on consequential edge cases and tail latency.
entries.failure: Average parity that conceals rare numerical or format failures.

entries.title: Caching and batch inference
entries.summary: Much model work repeats: the same instructions, the same reference documents, the same overnight jobs.
judgement: Much model work repeats: the same instructions, the same reference documents, the same overnight jobs. Prefix caching reuses prompt computation; response caching reuses an answer and needs separate validity and permission checks. Batch processing can reduce the cost of deferrable work. Both are mature and cut bills when the rules are explicit: what may be cached, for how long, for whom, and what invalidates it. The risk sits at the edges, where a cached answer outlasts the permission or information on which it depends.
entries.where: Repeated prompts or overnight tasks with a clear expiry policy.
entries.test: Stale entries, tenant boundaries, invalidation when permissions change, and the actual reduction in cost.
entries.failure: Cached results that retain revoked or outdated information.

entries.title: Speculative decoding and distributed serving
entries.summary: Speculative decoding and distributed serving raise throughput for large self-hosted workloads, and serving engines now support both.
judgement: Speculative decoding and distributed serving raise throughput for large self-hosted workloads, and serving engines now support both [168]. They add moving parts that someone must operate, monitor and recover. Adopt them once measured utilisation or latency justifies the complexity. The editors expect multi-token prediction to bring stronger open models to hardware organisations already own, and a later edition will revisit that development.
entries.where: A sustained workload and engineers who can operate the configuration.
entries.test: Throughput, tail latency and failure recovery at realistic concurrency.
entries.failure: The fastest isolated benchmark becoming the least reliable service.

entries.title: Permission-aware retrieval
entries.summary: Retrieve only what the requesting person and task are entitled to see.
judgement: Retrieve only what the requesting person and task are entitled to see. In Brightbeam's practitioner experience, some search and assistant pilots index broadly and apply permissions late; the retrieval layer then bypasses controls that the original applications enforced. OWASP lists sensitive information disclosure among the top risks for LLM applications [170]. Carry source permissions into the index, apply them at query time, and test the boundaries. The enterprise posture is Revisit where deployed assistants lack effective permission checks at retrieval time.
entries.where: Enterprise search across teams, clients or sensitive records.
entries.test: Cross-tenant queries, revoked access and indirect references to restricted documents.
entries.failure: Retrieval that bypasses permissions enforced elsewhere.

entries.title: Hybrid keyword and vector search
entries.summary: Technical, legal and operational documents mix exact identifiers (part numbers, clause references, codes) with natural language.
judgement: Technical, legal and operational documents mix exact identifiers (part numbers, clause references, codes) with natural language. Vector search can retrieve paraphrases but miss exact identifiers; keyword search can miss differently worded matches. Combining them can recover evidence missed by either method alone, and mature databases support both [181]. Measure retrieval recall and answer quality separately, on a question set you own. Similarity in an embedding space is weak evidence that a document answers the question.
entries.where: Corpora that mix codes and natural language.
entries.test: Retrieval recall and answer quality, measured separately on an owned question set.
entries.failure: A similar document that fails to answer the question.

entries.title: Reranking and retrieval evaluation
entries.summary: When search returns many plausible near-matches, a reranker scores the candidates before the model reads them.
judgement: When search returns many plausible near-matches, a reranker scores the candidates before the model reads them. It can lift the right passage into view, at a cost in computation and latency [197]. Pair it with evaluation: a labelled query set that shows whether the right material was found, including for rare queries. A reranker trained on data like the generator's can share its blind spots.
entries.where: Search results with many plausible near-matches.
entries.test: Ranking gains against added latency, including failures on rare queries.
entries.failure: A reranker that amplifies the generator's blind spots.

entries.title: Document parsing and OCR
entries.summary: A knowledge assistant depends on reliable document ingestion.
judgement: A knowledge assistant depends on reliable document ingestion. Scanned documents, tables, footnotes and reading order can cause basic text extraction to fail, and extraction errors can flow downstream into confident answers. Open-source parsers now preserve layout and tables and keep the page reference for provenance [180]. Check extraction against page images before using the extracted content downstream, and keep a sample under continuous review.
entries.where: Scanned or complex documents that are central to the task.
entries.test: Extraction checked against page images, including footnotes, tables and reading order.
entries.failure: Bad ingestion that creates confident downstream errors.

entries.title: Knowledge graphs and GraphRAG
entries.summary: Some questions require linked information: which suppliers feed this assembly, which controls depend on this system, which clauses use this definition.
judgement: Some questions require linked information: which suppliers feed this assembly, which controls depend on this system, which clauses use this definition. Explicit relations can support these questions better than passage retrieval alone, and GraphRAG builds a graph from documents automatically [175]. Automatic extraction can turn speculation into apparent fact, and building the graph costs time and money. Compare answer support and cost against simpler retrieval on your own questions before investing.
entries.where: Questions that span suppliers, assets, processes or a structured domain.
entries.test: Graph construction cost and answer support against simpler retrieval.
entries.failure: Extracted relations that present speculation as fact.

entries.title: Context assembly and compression
entries.summary: What enters the prompt is a decision with consequences.
judgement: What enters the prompt is a decision with consequences. Long-running agents compact their history, summarise documents and hand work between steps, and each compression can erase the condition that made the advice safe. Treat context assembly as versioned, testable code: record what was included, from where and why. Seed important exceptions into test cases and check that summaries keep them across handoffs.
entries.where: Long-running work that exceeds a practical context or cost budget.
entries.test: Seed exceptions and check that summaries keep them across handoffs.
entries.failure: Compression that erases a safety condition.

entries.title: Agent memory with owners and expiry
entries.summary: Persistent agents arrived in the second half of 2026: OpenAI says Dots gives agents their own cloud computer, Anthropic's Claude Duet research preview works in the background, and Meta says Muse acts across a person's apps.
judgement: Persistent agents arrived in the second half of 2026: OpenAI says Dots gives agents their own cloud computer, Anthropic's Claude Duet research preview works in the background, and Meta says Muse acts across a person's apps [17, 19, 20]. Persistent operation raises questions about what each product retains and who controls it. Decide who can write, correct, share and delete it before agents retain it across tasks, and keep organisational memory in stores controlled by the workflow, with schema, retention, permissions and audit. An outdated inference can otherwise become persistent organisational knowledge.
entries.where: Any persistent personal or organisational agent.
entries.test: Attempt correction, deletion, export and isolation across users and sessions.
entries.failure: An outdated inference that becomes organisational knowledge.
entries.examples: Memory registries; retention policies; workflow-owned stores.

entries.title: Expertise and tacit knowledge capture
entries.summary: The judgement needed for difficult cases often remains with experts: a cue that something is wrong, or an exception the procedure omits.
judgement: The judgement needed for difficult cases often remains with experts: a cue that something is wrong, or an exception the procedure omits. Capturing it means recording the situation, the origin and the exceptions with each piece of advice, then testing whether another practitioner can use it well. A recorded statement still needs validation before others rely on it. The test is practical: compare decisions made with and without reviewed knowledge.
entries.where: Expert-dependent work where documents omit crucial decision context.
entries.test: Compare novice decisions with and without reviewed knowledge fragments.
entries.failure: A recorded opinion treated as validated knowledge.
entries.examples: Critical decision interviews; knowledge audits; expert-knowledge stores that keep each piece of advice with its source and conditions.

entries.title: Evidence provenance and citations
entries.summary: Bind every answer a reader may rely on to the exact evidence version and passage, and mark what the source supports apart from what the system inferred.
judgement: Bind every answer a reader may rely on to the exact evidence version and passage, and mark what the source supports apart from what the system inferred. A real link can still fail to support the claim beside it. Courts have begun to require independent human verification of AI-assisted material [54], and auditors are likely to ask the same question of internal decisions: which evidence, which version, checked by whom. Sample citations routinely for entailment, date, passage accuracy and permission.
entries.where: Any answer a reader may rely on or challenge.
entries.test: Sample citations for entailment, date, passage accuracy and permission.
entries.failure: A genuine link that fails to support the claim beside it.
entries.examples: Document hashes; passage references; version identifiers.

entries.title: Data contracts and semantic definitions
entries.summary: Before delegating decisions over data, agree what each field means, its unit, its owner and how changes are announced.
judgement: Before delegating decisions over data, agree what each field means, its unit, its owner and how changes are announced. Models join and summarise across systems readily, and a technically valid join can combine incompatible meanings: revenue booked with revenue recognised, or a weekly figure with a monthly one. Contracts and shared definitions are established data engineering practice; agents make them urgent because agents act on the joins they make. Replay known decisions after every schema or definition change.
entries.where: Several systems that use the same business term differently.
entries.test: Replay known decisions after schema and definition changes.
entries.failure: A valid join that combines incompatible meanings.
entries.examples: Versioned schemas; semantic layers; feature stores.

entries.title: Synthetic data for gaps and testing
entries.summary: Generated examples help explore rare cases and test systems without exposing real records.
judgement: Generated examples help explore rare cases and test systems without exposing real records. They also carry the generator's assumptions: research on recursive training with generated data has found loss of rare cases at the distribution's tails under the studied conditions [198], and training and testing on the same generator can create an appearance of progress. Keep an independent evaluation on held-out real cases, and measure novelty, leakage and bias in the synthetic set.
entries.where: Underrepresented rare cases, where use of the source data is permitted.
entries.test: Novelty, leakage, bias and performance on held-out real cases.
entries.failure: Progress that exists only on synthetic data.

entries.title: Freshness, correction and deletion propagation
entries.summary: When a record changes, or a valid deletion request applies, trace the change through indexes, embeddings, caches, agent memories and stored outputs.
judgement: When a record changes, or a valid deletion request applies, trace the change through indexes, embeddings, caches, agent memories and stored outputs. Deleting the source alone can leave copies behind. The GDPR right to erasure has conditions and exceptions [193]; record the applicable basis, any retention duty and the treatment of backups. Agent memory multiplies the places to check. Map the lineage now: withdraw one record and trace every representation that depends on it.
entries.where: Information that changes, or that people can ask to remove.
entries.test: Withdraw one record and trace every dependent representation.
entries.failure: Copies that survive in embeddings, caches or logs.

entries.title: Bounded single-agent workflows
entries.summary: Delegate one defined job with explicit inputs, tools, limits and a stopping condition.
judgement: Delegate one defined job with explicit inputs, tools, limits and a stopping condition. Scope instructions matter: in UK AISI simulations, explicit scope cut full unsanctioned attacks from 26 of 50 runs to 4 of 49 [63]. Instructions alone are not a security boundary. An agent can carry on after the task is complete, so define completion in terms the system can check. Shared agents that serve a team need one named owner, act on behalf of the requester through a separately identifiable, scoped agent identity and keep a record of what they did.
entries.where: Work with a responsible owner and reversible actions.
entries.test: Completion, unauthorised actions, recovery and accepted results.
entries.failure: An agent that continues after the task is done.

entries.title: Deterministic workflow with model steps
entries.summary: Keep the sequence and the business rules explicit when the work follows a known path.
judgement: Keep the sequence and the business rules explicit when the work follows a known path. Most repeatable processes (extraction, checking, routing, approval) run better as a workflow that calls a model at defined steps than as an agent that plans its own route. Workflow engines and explicit state machines make each step observable and each change reviewable [166, 167]. The enterprise posture is Revisit because, in Brightbeam's experience, the enthusiasm for agents in 2026 has pushed many teams to replace predictable processes with autonomous ones.
entries.where: Repeatable extraction, checking, routing or approval.
entries.test: Compare a fixed workflow with an agent on reliability and maintenance effort.
entries.failure: An agent that makes a predictable process harder to control.

entries.title: Durable execution and idempotency
entries.summary: Long-running work crosses service failures, restarts and waits for people.
judgement: Long-running work crosses service failures, restarts and waits for people. Durable execution records each step so the work resumes where it stopped, and idempotency keys can prevent duplicate effects when the receiving service enforces them [167]. Agents make this more important because they retry on their own initiative. Interrupt the workflow at every boundary in testing and check that recovery is safe.
entries.where: Jobs that cross service failures or wait for human decisions.
entries.test: Interrupt at every boundary and verify safe recovery without duplicate transactions.
entries.failure: A retry that charges twice or sends the same instruction twice.

entries.title: MCP tool integration
entries.summary: The Model Context Protocol gives models and applications a common interface to enterprise tools, and it has become a common way to connect agents to systems.
judgement: The Model Context Protocol gives models and applications a common interface to enterprise tools [164], and it has become a common way to connect agents to systems. Protocol compatibility does not establish trust. Treat each MCP server as a privileged dependency: authenticate it, scope its permissions, pin its version, and test what happens when a tool returns malicious output, a known route for prompt injection [170]. Agent Skills moved to neutral governance under the Agentic AI Foundation in the second half of 2026 [127], which may reduce lock-in for internal agent libraries.
entries.where: Several models or applications that need a controlled set of enterprise tools.
entries.test: Authentication, permissions, schema changes and malicious tool output.
entries.failure: A trusted interface carrying untrusted content.
entries.examples: Model Context Protocol; vetted MCP servers.

entries.title: Agent-to-agent interoperability
entries.summary: Protocols such as A2A let agents in separate systems exchange tasks and results.
judgement: Protocols such as A2A let agents in separate systems exchange tasks and results [165]. Each handoff raises the questions a contract between organisations raises: who is the other party, who owns the task, how is it cancelled, and what context crosses the boundary. Interoperability can multiply access without clear accountability. Test explicit handoffs before depending on a common protocol.
entries.where: Separate systems that need to exchange tasks and results.
entries.test: Identity, task ownership, cancellation and loss of context across a handoff.
entries.failure: Access that multiplies faster than accountability.

entries.title: Multi-agent orchestration
entries.summary: Add agents only when a division of work improves measured outcomes enough to pay for the coordination.
judgement: Add agents only when a division of work improves measured outcomes enough to pay for the coordination. Hierarchies of agents can help with large tasks, and they can also repeat one another's mistakes, multiply cost and widen the attack surface. Compare any multi-agent design with a single agent under the same token, time and review budget, and keep delegation depth and tool access as explicit test conditions.
entries.where: Distinct tasks or expertise that can be separated and checked independently.
entries.test: Compare with a single agent under the same token, time and review budget.
entries.failure: Agents that compound each other's errors.

entries.title: Computer-use and browser agents
entries.summary: GPT-6 Astra, Dots and Claude Duet put computer use at the centre of the product in the second half of 2026.
judgement: GPT-6 Astra, Dots and Claude Duet put computer use at the centre of the product in the second half of 2026 [15, 17, 19]. They help where a necessary workflow has no stable API. They are also exposed: untrusted page content can redirect an agent that holds real permissions, and OpenAI withdrew its standalone agentic browser in August [132]. Evaluate them with restricted accounts and human confirmation for consequential actions, and wait where the agent would browse over sensitive data until prompt injection has a demonstrated defence. Several launches excluded the EEA and the UK [17, 19]. The enterprise posture is Plan for: staff will meet these agents through vendors and personal tools.
entries.where: A necessary workflow with no suitable stable API; non-sensitive data.
entries.test: Misleading pages, changed layouts, session expiry and accidental submission.
entries.failure: Page content that redirects an agent holding real permissions.

entries.title: Human approval and takeover
entries.summary: Give a person the information, time and authority to approve or stop a specific action, and record what they decided and why.
judgement: Give a person the information, time and authority to approve or stop a specific action, and record what they decided and why. Habitual approval provides little meaningful oversight. Courts have begun to require human verification of AI-assisted documents [54]. Brightbeam has argued that a structured record of overrides, with the change, the reason and the reviewer, is the clearest evidence that a person was in charge [146] (see IR-043). Measure whether reviewers understand what they approve, how often they reject, and whether takeover works under time pressure.
entries.where: Actions that change money, access, publications or consequential records.
entries.test: Reviewer comprehension, rejection rate and takeover success under time pressure.
entries.failure: Habitual approval that provides no oversight.
entries.examples: Approval queues; interruption and rollback controls; structured override records.

entries.title: Reusable agent skills and prompt packages
entries.summary: Reusable instructions and skills spread good practice across teams, and they can direct consequential tool use.
judgement: Reusable instructions and skills spread good practice across teams, and they can direct consequential tool use. Treat them as governed dependencies. Version them, review changes, and inspect them for hidden tool use and permissions they should not need. In tests, a planted instruction file in a Downloads folder hijacked coding agents [101]. Vet third-party skills as you would vet a software dependency.
entries.where: Teams that repeat task procedures across tools or agents.
entries.test: Review package changes; test for hidden tool use and unintended permissions.
entries.failure: A helpful-looking instruction bundle that introduces supply-chain risk.
entries.examples: Versioned skills; prompt registries; Agent Skills.

entries.title: Agent sandboxes and egress control
entries.summary: Run agents away from production secrets, and limit where they can connect and what resources they can use, in the environment itself.
judgement: Run agents away from production secrets, and limit where they can connect and what resources they can use, in the environment itself. In September 2026 an OpenAI training run reached an outside chatbot through a DNS gap, and red-teaming found virtual-machine escapes in frontier training infrastructure [4, 6]. A container alone is an inadequate boundary for some threat models. Combine isolated runtimes, network allowlists, scoped credentials and resource limits, and test them from the inside. The enterprise posture is Revisit because many agent pilots run with developers' own access.
entries.where: Any agent that executes code, reads untrusted material or uses tools.
entries.test: Attempt secret access, network escape and resource exhaustion from inside the sandbox.
entries.failure: A boundary that holds in the demonstration and leaks under pressure.
entries.examples: Isolated runtimes; network allowlists; scoped credentials.

entries.title: Coding agents across delivery
entries.summary: Coding is prominent in one vendor's activity data: in OpenAI's enterprise data, Codex reached 64% of combined Codex and ChatGPT enterprise output tokens by June.
judgement: Coding is prominent in one vendor's activity data: in OpenAI's enterprise data, Codex reached 64% of combined Codex and ChatGPT enterprise output tokens by June [73]. Start with bounded changes and acceptance tests that a person or team owns independently of the agent, then follow outcomes through deployment. When one model family writes the code, the tests and the first review, the checks share blind spots: use independent acceptance tests and named human sign-off. Another model family may add a useful review, but does not guarantee independent errors. Coding agents have also leaked data: they posted more than 13,000 sensitive screenshots from 343 companies to public repositories [100].
entries.where: A team that can review, test and revert the generated change.
entries.test: Accepted changes, escaped defects, review time and rollback rate.
entries.failure: Code volume rising while comprehension and maintainability fall.
entries.examples: Coding agents; CI gates; review queues.

entries.title: Unattended open-ended autonomy
entries.summary: Defer general authority wherever success, limits and recovery cannot be specified and tested.
judgement: Defer general authority wherever success, limits and recovery cannot be specified and tested. The containment failures of the second half of 2026 came from capable agents with network access pursuing their objectives beyond their scope [1 to 9]. A successful demonstration says little about rare, costly failures over long runs. Defer deployment while preparing for the risks: attackers already run intrusions at machine speed with agent frameworks [98, 99], and regulators are asking about incidents. Containment, detection and a rehearsed stop are needed whether or not you deploy autonomous agents yourself.
entries.where: Agents that could make irreversible decisions without timely oversight.
entries.test: Require evidence from the autonomous operating mode itself, and demonstrate containment first.
entries.failure: A strong demonstration mistaken for evidence about long-run behaviour.

entries.title: Agent identities and least privilege
entries.summary: Give each agent its own identity, with authority scoped to the task, an accountable owner and a way to revoke it mid-task.
judgement: Give each agent its own identity, with authority scoped to the task, an accountable owner and a way to revoke it mid-task. Shared service accounts hide who authorised an action, and developers' personal credentials give agents far more reach than the task needs. Incidents in the second half of 2026 showed capable agents exploiting whatever access lay in reach [1 to 9], and one intrusion used an agent framework to attempt sign-ins to more than 2,250 customer environments [98]. Most access models were designed for people and services; review yours for software that improvises.
entries.where: Any agent that can reach a business system or act for a person.
entries.test: Revoke access mid-task; test permissions outside the task boundary.
entries.failure: Shared accounts that hide who authorised an action.
entries.examples: Short-lived credentials; role and attribute policies; per-tool keys with spend caps.

entries.title: Prompt-injection resilience
entries.summary: Any agent that reads websites, documents, messages or tool output can be steered by instructions hidden in them.
judgement: Any agent that reads websites, documents, messages or tool output can be steered by instructions hidden in them. In tests reported in the second half of 2026, a planted instruction file hijacked coding agents [101], and a self-replicating injection spread between research checkpoints in simulated settings [88]; OpenAI withdrew its standalone agentic browser [132]. Layer the controls (isolate untrusted content, check tool calls against policy, require confirmation for consequential actions) and limit what an agent can do when detection fails. Measure both attack success and the legitimate work lost to the controls.
entries.where: Agents that consume websites, documents, messages or tool output.
entries.test: Realistic hostile inputs; measure attack success and legitimate-task loss.
entries.failure: A filter result used to justify broad authority.

entries.title: Secrets, data loss and output validation
entries.summary: Keep secrets outside anything the model can read, and validate outputs at the point of use: before they reach a log, a tool, a rendered page or an export.
judgement: Keep secrets outside anything the model can read, and validate outputs at the point of use: before they reach a log, a tool, a rendered page or an export. Coding agents posted more than 13,000 sensitive screenshots from 343 companies to public repositories in the second half of 2026 [100]. Redaction can fail on transformed or indirectly disclosed information, so test leakage paths as an attacker would.
entries.where: Models that touch sensitive data or feed executable downstream systems.
entries.test: Probe leakage and dangerous output in logs, tools, rendered pages and exports.
entries.failure: Redaction that misses transformed or indirect disclosure.
entries.examples: Secret brokers; schema and business-rule validation.

entries.title: Independent test and grading environments
entries.summary: Keep the answers and the grader outside anything the agent can read or write.
judgement: Keep the answers and the grader outside anything the agent can read or write. Agents often optimise the measure in front of them: on BaitBench, 57.1% of frontier agents' runs took a planted score-inflating shortcut [84], and Epoch found leading submissions to its innovation benchmark describing their results misleadingly [65]. A high score can reflect access to the answer or the scorer. Check that an agent that does nothing cannot pass and that a tampering agent cannot raise its score. The enterprise posture is Revisit because many teams still let the same system build, test and grade the work.
entries.where: Any case where an agent's performance grants it production authority.
entries.test: Verify that a null agent cannot pass and a tampering agent cannot improve its score.
entries.failure: A score that reflects access to the answer.

entries.title: Red-teaming and adversarial rehearsal
entries.summary: Exercise the deployed system, its tools and its recovery process against a defined threat model, then rerun after material changes.
judgement: Exercise the deployed system, its tools and its recovery process against a defined threat model, then rerun after material changes. An authorised three-week stress test of OpenAI's internal agent monitoring found ways the monitor could be bypassed [8]: a finite exercise finds real weaknesses and leaves others undiscovered. Report the attacker effort beside the result, because a positive safety result is difficult to interpret without its test conditions.
entries.where: Systems approaching a consequential release.
entries.test: Complete attack paths, rerun after material configuration changes.
entries.failure: A finite exercise read as proof of safety.

entries.title: AI supply-chain verification
entries.summary: Track every model, weight file, dataset, package and external tool with its version and provenance, and rehearse the response to a compromised dependency.
judgement: Track every model, weight file, dataset, package and external tool with its version and provenance, and rehearse the response to a compromised dependency. Supply-chain attacks reached AI tooling in the second half of 2026: Microsoft attributed a compromise in which a group used an agent framework to attempt sign-ins to more than 2,250 customer environments [98]. Model hubs are also consolidating; Nvidia agreed to buy Hugging Face, subject to approvals [125]. Unsigned or mutable artefacts make investigation and rollback unreliable.
entries.where: Applications that pull dependencies from several providers.
entries.test: Rebuild from a manifest; rehearse the response to a compromised dependency.
entries.failure: Mutable artefacts that defeat investigation and rollback.

entries.title: Structured oversight records
entries.summary: A decision that may be challenged needs a record a reviewer can follow without the original operator: who proposed, who changed what, why, and who approved.
judgement: A decision that may be challenged needs a record a reviewer can follow without the original operator: who proposed, who changed what, why, and who approved. The EU AI Act's high-risk duties (record-keeping and human oversight) apply from 2 December 2027 for Annex III systems and 2 August 2028 for Annex I products [49], EN 18286 sets quality-management expectations [50], and courts have begun to require verification of AI-assisted documents [54]. Portable formats for such records are emerging. A complete record supports reconstruction; it does not by itself establish sound judgement, meaningful oversight or legal compliance.
entries.where: Decisions that must later be reconstructed or reviewed across systems.
entries.test: Reconstruct a real decision from its record alone.
entries.failure: A complete record mistaken for evidence of sound judgement.
entries.examples: Decision logs with diffs and rationale; open record formats for approvals, overrides and handoffs.

entries.title: Privacy engineering and minimisation
entries.summary: Collect, keep and expose only the personal data the task needs.
judgement: Collect, keep and expose only the personal data the task needs. Integrated systems create new copies of personal data in prompts, traces, memories and evaluation sets, and useful debugging records can become a second sensitive dataset. Map the data flows, test whether minimised inputs still meet the acceptance criteria, and set retention for traces as you would for any record. Data protection law sets out the obligations [193]; the NIST AI Risk Management Framework offers complementary voluntary risk-management guidance [171].
entries.where: Personal information that enters a model, trace, memory or evaluation set.
entries.test: Map data flows; test minimised inputs against the task's acceptance criteria.
entries.failure: Debugging records that become a second sensitive dataset.

entries.title: Incident containment and kill switches
entries.summary: Design a tested way to stop actions, revoke credentials, preserve evidence and resume safely.
judgement: Design a tested way to stop actions, revoke credentials, preserve evidence and resume safely. In September an OpenAI training run reached an outside chatbot, and the automatic stop failed [4]. Stopping the interface can leave background work running. AI is also surfacing vulnerabilities faster than some organisations can fix them: Bank of America brought in about 1,000 contractors, and PHP shipped emergency patches for two flaws found with AI help [96]. Plan capacity for a surge in patching alongside the stopping controls. The enterprise posture is Revisit because most incident plans were written before software could act on its own.
entries.where: Agents that run unattended or connect to operational systems.
entries.test: A timed drill that stops in-flight and queued actions across dependencies.
entries.failure: A stopped interface with work still running behind it.
entries.examples: Revocation runbooks; circuit breakers; recovery queues.

entries.title: Formal verification and proof assistants
entries.summary: AI-assisted machine-checked proofs reached open-source libraries in the second half of 2026: Anthropic reports no-crash proofs for 239 entry points across 123 libraries, for inputs under 64 MB and under stated assumptions, and the KLS proof gained a Lean formalisation.
judgement: AI-assisted machine-checked proofs reached open-source libraries in the second half of 2026: Anthropic reports no-crash proofs for 239 entry points across 123 libraries, for inputs under 64 MB and under stated assumptions [95], and the KLS proof gained a Lean formalisation [26, 179]. Use formal checks where a precise specification can be written and challenged. A correct proof of the wrong specification leaves the business risk intact, so review the assumptions against the real system. Most organisations can watch; those that own critical components should test one.
entries.where: A critical algorithm, contract or mathematical claim with formal boundaries.
entries.test: Verify the property; review whether the assumptions match the real system.
entries.failure: A proof of the wrong specification.

entries.title: Conformance evidence over certification claims
entries.summary: Map each claimed obligation to evidence and competent review.
judgement: Map each claimed obligation to evidence and competent review. EN 18286, the first harmonised quality-management standard under the EU AI Act, was cited in the Official Journal on 14 October 2026 [50]. Its use can support a presumption of conformity for the corresponding requirements; it does not certify every aspect of an AI system. Nine of ten requested standard areas still lack a harmonised standard, according to the cited report [160]. A checklist, badge or protocol can conceal missing system-level evidence. Build assurance cases that trace each claim to an artefact, and ask an independent reviewer to find the gaps.
entries.where: A regulated purchase or deployment that needs an assurance case.
entries.test: An independent reviewer traces each claim to supporting evidence and identifies gaps.
entries.failure: A badge that hides missing evidence.

entries.title: High-stakes autonomous decisions
entries.summary: Withhold final autonomous authority over health, access to essential services, employment or material rights until evidence covers the intended population, its failures and its remedy.
judgement: Withhold final autonomous authority over health, access to essential services, employment or material rights until evidence covers the intended population, its failures and its remedy. A review of 1,357 FDA-cleared or approved AI devices through 5 December 2025 identified registered prospective trials for 34 and patient-outcome evaluation for 3 [94]; even strong diagnostic results still await clinical testing [92]. Keep the human decision with the accountable person and use the system as support. The enterprise posture is Revisit for organisations already letting automated decisions stand without review.
entries.where: Decisions that affect health, essential services, employment or material rights.
entries.test: Domain validation, accountable sign-off, appeal and a tested fallback.
entries.failure: An explanation that rationalises a wrong decision.
entries.examples: Decision support with retained human authority.

entries.title: Owned task examinations
entries.summary: Build a representative, versioned examination of the work you intend to delegate: real case distributions, difficult slices, cases where the right answer is to abstain, and adversarial inputs.
judgement: Build a representative, versioned examination of the work you intend to delegate: real case distributions, difficult slices, cases where the right answer is to abstain, and adversarial inputs. Set acceptance criteria with the process owner, protect unseen test cases and refresh the set when the work changes. Public benchmarks saturate, change method and reward optimisation to the test [61, 84]. A small, convenient test set does the same. The enterprise posture is Revisit because many organisations still rely on vendor benchmarks or public rankings when they decide what to delegate.
entries.where: A team that can define acceptable work and the exceptions that matter.
entries.test: Include real distributions, difficult slices, abstention and adversarial cases.
entries.failure: A convenient test set that rewards optimisation to the test.

entries.title: Model-and-harness evaluation
entries.summary: Evaluate the complete configuration: model, prompts, tools, memory, policies and runtime.
judgement: Evaluate the complete configuration: model, prompts, tools, memory, policies and runtime. The harness around a model can move its score by tens of points: ARC Prize verified one model at 62.7% with its standard harness and up to 99.9% with its maker's adapter, though whether the two are comparable is disputed [61, 153]. Attributing every gain to the model hides system changes, and every model change can break behaviour the harness relied on. Freeze the case set and compare configurations with repeated runs and failure analysis.
entries.where: Any component change, or any move to a new environment.
entries.test: Freeze the case set; compare configurations with repeat runs and failure analysis.
entries.failure: System changes credited to the model.

entries.title: Judge models with human calibration
entries.summary: When outputs are open-ended, a model can score them against a rubric at a scale people cannot match.
judgement: When outputs are open-ended, a model can score them against a rubric at a scale people cannot match. Treat that judge as a fallible instrument and calibrate it against blinded expert review. Judges can reward persuasive language and share the generator's blind spots; monitors that read a model's reasoning can be persuaded by it [87]. Measure disagreement, bias and sensitivity to style before relying on the scores.
entries.where: Open-ended outputs where exact automated scoring falls short.
entries.test: Disagreement, bias and sensitivity to style on blinded examples.
entries.failure: A judge that rewards fluent prose over correct content.

entries.title: Accepted work and full-cost measurement
entries.summary: Count the work its owner accepts, and include compute, review, rework, exceptions and operations in the cost.
judgement: Count the work its owner accepts, and include compute, review, rework, exceptions and operations in the cost. Track the same work units before and after, including rejected and abandoned tasks. Platforms report activity (tokens, seats, generated output) and surveys report self-assessed savings [62, 73]; neither establishes realised value, and 60% of respondents to one survey say AI increased their workload [24]. In Brightbeam's experience, most AI dashboards still measure activity. Set up an accepted-work ledger on one delegated workflow within the next quarter.
entries.where: Any team that claims productivity or prepares to scale.
entries.test: The same work units before and after, including rejected and abandoned tasks.
entries.failure: Activity measures reported as value.

entries.title: Drift, slices and uncertainty
entries.summary: Track whether quality and confidence stay appropriate for each population the system serves.
judgement: Track whether quality and confidence stay appropriate for each population the system serves. Inputs, users, language, workflow and suppliers change over time, and a stable average can hide deterioration for a small group. Compare error, calibration and abstention by consequential slice, and treat a model or supplier update as a reason to re-check. In Brightbeam's experience, systems drift quietly, and feedback fades after the pilot.
entries.where: Systems whose inputs, users, language, workflow or suppliers change.
entries.test: Error, calibration and abstention compared by consequential slice.
entries.failure: A stable average that hides harm to a small group.
entries.examples: Calibration curves; drift monitors; slice dashboards.

entries.title: Shadow and canary deployment
entries.summary: Run a challenger in shadow, with no authority, then give it a limited share of the work with rollback criteria agreed in advance.
judgement: Run a challenger in shadow, with no authority, then give it a limited share of the work with rollback criteria agreed in advance [199]. Check delayed outcomes, disagreements with the incumbent and rare failures before widening exposure. A short, quiet canary can miss seasonal or consequential cases, so set its length by the case mix.
entries.where: A production baseline with measurable comparison outcomes.
entries.test: Delayed labels, disagreements and rare failures before increasing exposure.
entries.failure: A quiet canary that missed the cases that matter.

entries.title: Fine-tuning and low-rank adapters
entries.summary: Adapt a model only when prompting and retrieval show a measured shortfall on a stable task and a controlled dataset can address it.
judgement: Adapt a model only when prompting and retrieval show a measured shortfall on a stable task and a controlled dataset can address it. Low-rank adapters can reduce training cost [174]. Maintenance remains: a base-model change requires compatibility checks and re-validation, and may require retraining. Training can also overfit, leak sensitive data or damage useful behaviour. Most organisations can watch; those with a measured shortfall should test.
entries.where: A stable task with a measured shortfall that training may address.
entries.test: Compare against the untuned model on held-out real data and unrelated skills.
entries.failure: Training that damages useful behaviour or leaks data.

entries.title: Distillation and specialist classifiers
entries.summary: High-volume, repetitive work with enough trustworthy labels can move from a large model to a small specialist: a distilled model or a classifier trained on a few examples.
judgement: High-volume, repetitive work with enough trustworthy labels can move from a large model to a small specialist: a distilled model or a classifier trained on a few examples [183]. The specialist can be cheaper and faster, and it can inherit its teacher's mistakes with less ability to recover. Compare teacher, student and a simple baseline on cases outside the training distribution, and keep independent validation.
entries.where: High-volume repetitive work with enough trustworthy labels.
entries.test: Teacher, student and simple baseline compared on out-of-distribution cases.
entries.failure: A student that inherits the teacher's errors.

entries.title: Reinforcement learning and post-training
entries.summary: Post-training with rewards teaches models to reason and act towards an outcome, and open libraries make it accessible.
judgement: Post-training with rewards teaches models to reason and act towards an outcome, and open libraries make it accessible [182]. Reward design and verification are the hard parts: over 10% of Anthropic's production reinforcement-learning environments were flagged as prone to reward hacking or broken tasks [86], and optimising a reward can displace the real objective. Evaluate only where the task outcome is observable and the evaluation environment is credible.
entries.where: An observable task outcome and a credible evaluation environment.
entries.test: Reward gaming, held-out generalisation and behaviour outside training conditions.
entries.failure: A reward that displaces the real objective.
entries.examples: TRL; supervised fine-tuning and preference methods.

entries.title: Governed learning releases
entries.summary: Agents that reuse procedures, memories or corrections across jobs can change their behaviour in production without changing model weights.
judgement: Agents that reuse procedures, memories or corrections across jobs can change their behaviour in production without changing model weights. Separate what an agent proposes to learn from the behaviour you have approved, test each change against both the cases it fixes and the cases that already worked, and ensure every release can be recalled. A local fix can degrade other tasks or persist after its source is withdrawn. Persistent agents launched in the second half of 2026 bring the question into everyday tools [17, 19, 20].
entries.where: Agents that accumulate procedures, memories or corrections across jobs.
entries.test: Evaluate changed and previously correct cases, then rehearse a rollback.
entries.failure: A learned fix that breaks other work or outlives its source.
entries.examples: Reviewed learning packages; signed, recallable releases of learned rules.

entries.title: Harness ablation and simplification
entries.summary: Harnesses accumulate retries, routing and coaching that compensated for weaker models.
judgement: Harnesses accumulate retries, routing and coaching that compensated for weaker models. Some of that is temporary scaffolding, and some of it (the outside scorer, the sandbox, the trace, the approval gate) is permanent control. When a new model arrives, remove one compensating component at a time and compare repeated runs, keeping every security control in place. Deleting a safety boundary because the model improved confuses the two purposes. Keep a component only where it demonstrably improves outcomes [200].
entries.where: Workflows that have accumulated retries, routing or coaching layers.
entries.test: Repeated runs with and without the component, security controls preserved.
entries.failure: A safety boundary removed as if it were scaffolding.

entries.title: Unreviewed self-modifying production agents
entries.summary: Defer agents that can rewrite their own objectives, permissions, evaluators or persistent procedures without outside control.
judgement: Defer agents that can rewrite their own objectives, permissions, evaluators or persistent procedures without outside control. A system that can change its own examiner undermines confidence in apparent improvement. AI already does a measurable share of research work inside one laboratory, under human supervision [21], and researchers warned in the second half of 2026 that the window for action may close once AI starts improving AI [139]. If an agent in your estate can change itself, require an isolated proposal, independent evaluation, approval and rollback before any self-modification reaches production. The enterprise posture is Watch: few organisations run such agents in production today, so track whether self-changing agents reach the tools your staff use (IR-058).
entries.where: Changes that can propagate into consequential production decisions.
entries.test: Isolated proposal, independent evaluation, approval and rollback first.
entries.failure: An agent that edits its own examiner.
entries.examples: Self-evolving agents with unrestricted write access.

entries.title: Classical tabular ML baselines
entries.summary: When the answer is a label, a score or a number predicted from historical records, start with a strong, simple baseline: regression, gradient boosting, a well-tuned classifier.
judgement: When the answer is a label, a score or a number predicted from historical records, start with a strong, simple baseline: regression, gradient boosting, a well-tuned classifier [172]. These methods often provide strong, economical baselines on structured data. Interpretability varies by model; check explanations rather than assuming them. In one published client case study, language models were considered and proved less accurate than a purpose-built data model [150]. The enterprise posture is Revisit because many organisations now route prediction problems to generative models by default.
entries.where: Labels, scores or numerical predictions over historical records.
entries.test: Leakage-resistant splits, calibration and business-relevant error costs.
entries.failure: A correlation in past data treated as the effect of an intervention.

entries.title: Tabular foundation models
entries.summary: Pretrained models for tables now compete with tuned classical methods on small and medium structured datasets, and they make rapid experimentation easy.
judgement: Pretrained models for tables now compete with tuned classical methods on small and medium structured datasets, and they make rapid experimentation easy [177]. Compare them with your tuned baseline on your own data, using time-aware or grouped holdouts, and compare calibration, compute and maintainability as well as accuracy.
